Also I should test a worst-case adversarial image: 400001 rows and 1M queries. The above is 391961 rows — close to worst case. Good.

Now, edge cases and error handling tests. Let me write a comprehensive test script:

A. Build errors:
1. FIB with /65 → error 2.
2. FIB with /128 → error.
3. Duplicate normalized prefix (same net+len, different hop) → error.
4. Duplicate normalized prefix with the SAME hop → error.
5. Duplicate that differs only in host bits (e.g., "2001:db8::1/32 5" and "2001:db8::2/32 5") → error.
6. Missing '/' → error.
7. Non-digit prefix length ("abc", "+3", "-1", "3x", "") → error.
8. Next hop too large (4294967296) → error; negative → error; "+5" → error.
9. Extra tokens (3 fields) → error.
10. Single field → error.
11. Invalid IPv6 (IPv4-only "1.2.3.4/32 5", zone id, "::1/64/8"?) → error.
12. Empty file → success, image with 1 row.
13. File of only blank lines → success, 1 row.
14. Comment line "# foo" → error.
15. Nonexistent FIB → error 2, no destination created.
16. Destination in a nonexistent directory → error.
17. FIB with a line > 256 bytes → we accept up to 64 KiB... The spec says lines at most 256 bytes are supported; longer may be rejected. We accept them if valid. That's fine (lenient).

Also check: build must leave an existing destination unchanged on failure. Test: create dest with content, run a failing build, verify unchanged.

B. Lookup errors:
1. Malformed image variants (each rule).
2. Bad trace lines.
3. Bad batch sizes: "", "0", "257", "abc", "+3", " 3", "3 ", "3x", "0x3", "-1", "0000" (value 0 → invalid), "0001" → 1 valid.
4. Wrong arg counts, unknown mode, extra args for scalar.
5. Empty trace → no output, rc 0.
6. Trace with only blank lines → no output.
7. Batch size not dividing trace length → still all records.

C. Format checks: image output exactness, no trailing spaces, LF endings, final newline, 16 lowercase hex.

#!/bin/bash

pass=0; fail=0
chk_err() {  # chk_err NAME expected_rc -- cmd...
  local name="$1"; shift
  out=$("$@" 2>$T/e.txt >$T/o.txt); rc=$?
  if [ $rc -ne 2 ]; then echo "FAIL[$name]: rc=$rc (want 2)"; head -c 200 $T/e.txt; fail=$((fail+1)); return; fi
  if [ -s $T/o.txt ]; then echo "FAIL[$name]: stdout not empty"; fail=$((fail+1)); return; fi
  if ! head -c 7 $T/e.txt | grep -q '^ERROR:'; then echo "FAIL[$name]: stderr does not start with ERROR:"; head -c 120 $T/e.txt; fail=$((fail+1)); return; fi
  if [ $(wc -c <$T/e.txt) -gt 1000000 ]; then echo "FAIL[$name]: stderr too big"; fail=$((fail+1)); return; fi
  pass=$((pass+1))
}
chk_ok() { local name="$1"; shift
  "$@" >$T/o.txt 2>$T/e.txt; rc=$?
